fullPassage:
Have you ever tried a combination of foods that seems strange but actually tastes amazing? Some food pairings may sound odd at first, but once you try them, you’ll wonder why you hadn’t tried them sooner. Let’s explore some of the world’s most unusual food pairings that actually work.

Hawaiian pizza is one of the most divisive foods in the world. People either love it or hate it. This pizza topped with ham and pineapple was invented in 1962 by Sam Panopoulos, a Greek immigrant living in Canada. He decided to put canned pineapple on pizza just to try something different. The combination of salty ham and sweet pineapple turned out to be a hit, and Hawaiian pizza quickly spread across North America. To this day, however, it remains a subject of heated debate: Is pineapple an acceptable pizza topping, or is it a crime against Italian cuisine?

Mango with sticky rice is a beloved dessert in Thailand. Interestingly, neither the mango nor the sticky rice is originally native to Thailand. Mangoes are believed to have originated in South Asia, while sticky rice has its roots in Southeast and East Asia. The dish represents the rich mixing of cultures that has taken place in Southeast Asia over centuries. Sweet, ripe mangoes are served on top of warm sticky rice, which is cooked in coconut milk. The creamy sweetness of the coconut rice pairs perfectly with the fresh, juicy mango, making it a favorite treat for both locals and tourists.

The Elvis is a sandwich made of peanut butter, banana, and bacon. It is named after Elvis Presley, the legendary rock and roll singer, who was known to be a huge fan of this unusual combination. Some people might think this sandwich is unhealthy, but it is actually quite nutritious. Peanut butter provides protein and healthy fats, bananas offer potassium and vitamins, and bacon adds a savory, salty crunch. Together, these ingredients create a balance of sweet, salty, and rich flavors that is surprisingly satisfying.

What makes these food pairings work so well? In many cases, it’s the contrast of flavors — sweet and salty, creamy and crunchy — that creates a memorable eating experience. The next time you encounter a food pairing that seems odd, don’t dismiss it right away. It might just be that you haven’t experienced it yet.

Curry is one of the most popular dishes in the world, enjoyed in many different forms across various cultures. Japanese curry, for example, is quite different from Indian curry. It is milder, sweeter, and thicker, often served over rice with meat and vegetables. Indian curry, on the other hand, tends to be more complex in flavor, using a wider variety of spices. The word "curry" is believed to come from the Tamil word "kari," which means sauce. Interestingly, Korean curry was influenced not directly by India but by Japan. During the early 20th century, curry was introduced to Korea through Japanese cuisine and has since become a popular comfort food in Korean households.

It is milder, sweeter, and thicker, often served over rice with meat and vegetables. Indian curry, on the other hand, tends to be more complex in flavor, using a wider variety of spices. The word "curry" is believed to come from the Tamil word "kari," which means sauce. Interestingly, Korean curry was influenced not directly by India but by Japan. During the early 20th century, curry was introduced to Korea through Japanese cuisine and has since become a popular comfort food in Korean households.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Korean curry was influenced by Japan, not directly by India."

det.korean: "Korean curry was influenced not directly by India but by Japan." → 한국 커리는 인도가 아닌 일본의 영향을 받았다. → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: 본문 "influenced not directly by India but by Japan"과 진술이 일치
det.tip: not A but B: A가 아니라 B → 진술의 핵심 구조와 대조

questions.passage: The Elvis is a sandwich made of peanut butter, banana, and bacon. It is named after Elvis Presley, the legendary rock and roll singer, who was known to be a huge fan of this unusual combination. Some people might think this sandwich is unhealthy, but it is actually quite nutritious. Peanut butter provides protein and healthy fats, bananas offer potassium and vitamins, and bacon adds a savory, salty crunch. Together, these ingredients create a balance of sweet, salty, and rich flavors that is surprisingly satisfying.
questions.stem:

"The Elvis sandwich is named after Elvis Presley because he invented the recipe."

det.korean: 본문: "named after Elvis Presley, the legendary rock and roll singer, who was known to be a huge fan of this unusual combination" → Elvis Presley가 레시피를 발명한 것이 아니라 이 조합의 열렬한 팬이었기 때문에 이름이 붙여졌다. → False
det.analysis:
❌ False: Elvis Presley는 이 샌드위치의 "huge fan"이었을 뿐, "invented the recipe"라는 내용은 없음
이름의 유래 = 팬이었기 때문(✓) ≠ 발명했기 때문(✗)
